text:
infra-bot: [ALERT] apiserver 503 spike in us-west1; rate=~120/min over last 5m; affected: api-proxy pool; possible provisioning backlog :rotating_light:
maya: seeing large attach latencies for nvidia-gpu pools, provisioner logs showing retries, controller-manager queue growing :confused:
maya: paste logs below
```
E0312 14:02:01.123 controller.go:218] attach volume failed: rpc timeout (10s)
E0312 14:02:01.456 kubelet_attach.go:87] attach for device gpu-rtx failed: attach API 504
I0312 14:02:03.000 provisioner.go:543] enqueueing node for attach retry, retryCount=3
```
bryce: timeline? did the routing change or NAT gateway flip?
anya: cloud provider reported a transient SNAT exhaustion earlier at 13:58 but claimed cleared at 14:05. still, attach RPCs are 5xxing to the attach service.
sam: controller-manager metrics show `workqueue_depth` for `attach-controller` jumped from 12 -> 420 between 13:55-14:05.
maya: confirmed. also apiserver error rate aligns with attach backpressure; apiserver proxy threads block while waiting for attach responses.
bryce: can we throttle onboarding/scale down rollout? which DEPLOY is rolling currently?
maya: deployment redwood/gpu-models v3.2.1 had a canary between 13:50-14:10 (autoscale to ~60 pods). suspect spike from canary pushing many new GPU pod attaches.
anya: quick mitigation options:
- pause canary autoscaler (scale to 1)
- increase provisioner concurrency to allow more attach workers (but risks more SNAT)
- route attach RPCs via east-west LB instead of NAT (needs infra change)
sam: short term: pause canary and drain pending pods to a holding node pool (no GPU attach). i'll pause HPA.
maya: doing `kubectl scale deploy/gpu-models-canary --replicas=1 -n redwood` now
```
kubectl scale deploy/gpu-models-canary -n redwood --replicas=1
```
infra-bot: action recorded: HPA pause requested by sam at 14:07
bryce: after pause, what's the plan to clear backlog? we have lots of stuck attach tasks consuming controller-manager workers. ideas?
anya: recommended: run a targeted `workqueue_requeue` to re-enqueue failing items with exponential backoff reset; also consider bumping controller-manager `--max-requests-inflight` to avoid head-of-line blocking.
sam: can we inspect provisioner logs for error signatures to avoid blind requeues?
maya: log sample shows `rpc timeout` then `context deadline exceeded` with stacktrace toward attach client. likely NAT conntrack exhaustion causing late TCP failures.
bryce: cost note: switching to dedicated east-west LB will add $0.03/hr per node but will drastically reduce SNAT pressure. ops: we should budget for this for high-onboard windows.
anya: for now, increase NAT port pool by resizing nodes from /27 -> /26? that's infra heavy. try backlog drain + pause rollout + graceful attach retries.
maya: monitoring: created a dashboard for attach latency + workqueue depth, and set alert: if attach lat > 5s for 10m -> page oncall.
sam: rolling mitigation in place, will follow up in 30m. if apiserver 5xxs persist after backlog clears, escalate to network.
bryce: thanks. also file a postmortem note and cost-impact calc for Dedicated LB proposal.
maya: noted. cc @anya on follow-up runbook edits and HPA guardrails for future canaries. :thumbsup:
